item.title: Carney approval high in Sask., Liberals at 49 per cent national voter support: poll
item.description: Western provinces showed high approval ratings for Mark Carney, at 53 per cent for Alberta and 59 per cent for Manitoba and Saskatchewan.

item.title: Warm to early sounds of spring: Five things to do this weekend in Saskatoon, March 6-8
item.description: Take in a musical book launch, a 1950s-style concert, a Canadian concert tour, orchestral music for spring and a Ukrainian comedy show.

item.title: Driver could face fines, charges after semi's cargo smashes Saskatoon overpass
item.description: The semi trailer "was too high for the structure and caused significant damage," police said.

item.title: Despite off-night shooting, Huskies advance to women's hoops semifinal
item.description: Though the University of Saskatchewan Huskies were off-target on the offensive end, they were sharp enough defensively to make up for it as they began their pursuit for back-to-back national basketball titles.

item.title: Opinion: Saskatchewan needs to deal with its massive debt
item.description: The government has been overspending its own budget plans for years. It spent $970 million more than budgeted in 2024. In 2023, the government went over budget by $2.2 billion. In 2022, it was $1.4 billion. And in 2021, it was $2.5 billion.

item.title: Five Saskatoon concerts to see in March
item.description: Check out a variety of local concerts this month from country to Newfoundland folk and pop to funk.

item.title: Opinion: Saskatchewan government should reduce record spending in budget
item.description: Rather than continue riding the resource rollercoaster, the Moe government should instead seek to align permanent spending with more reliable stable sources of government revenue.

item.title: Opinion: If Ottawa doesn't reform supply management, Washington will
item.description: Supply management serves legitimate policy objectives: territorial occupation, income stability, and a degree of food sovereignty. But it is currently too rigid and too costly. The system needs modernization, not blind defence.

item.title: Weekend Roundup: Huskie women's basketball team repeats as national champions
item.description: The Saskatchewan Huskies are Bronze Baby winners again.
